style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The royal wedding song -- 'a song of love' set to 'The Lilies' -- and the psalm the letter to the Hebrews quotes to prove that the Son is God: 'Your throne, O God, is forever and ever.' The poet's heart bubbles over like a pot; his tongue is a scribe's pen. He praises the King first -- fairer than the sons of men, grace poured on his lips, a sword on his thigh, riding out for truth and humility and righteousness, arrows in the hearts of his enemies -- and then says what no court poet could say of a merely human king: Your throne, O God, is forever; You love righteousness and hate wickedness, so God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness beyond Your companions. Then the bride: kings' daughters in the court, the queen in gold of Ophir at his right hand, and the counsel the church has long read to brides and to itself as the Bride -- forget your people and your father's house; the King desires your beauty; bow to him, for he is your lord. She is led in with her companions in embroidered robes, and the psalm ends with sons who will be princes and a name remembered in every generation. Israel sang it for a Davidic king's wedding; the church sings it for the Bridegroom and His bride.

1.text: For the choir director, set to 'The Lilies.' Of the sons of Korah, a maskil; a song of love. My heart is bubbling over with a good theme; I recite my verses to the King; my tongue is the pen of a skilled scribe.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Shoshannim [shushan -- lilies], for the sons [ben] of Korah [Qorach], Maschil ['of instruction', maskil, the KJV margin], A Song [shir] of loves [yedid -- love, beloved]. My heart [leb] is inditing ['boileth, or, bubbleth up', rachash, the KJV margin] a good [tov] matter [dabar]: I speak [amar] of the things which I have made [maaseh] touching the king [melek]: my tongue [lashon] is the pen [et] of a ready [mahir -- quick, skilled] writer [saphar -- scribe].
1.notes: shir yedidot (H7892, H3039): a song of loves -- the Psalter's one wedding psalm; the tune shoshannim (H7799), 'lilies'. rachash libbi dabar tov (H7370, H3820, H1697, H2896): the margin's 'boileth' -- the heart bubbling like a pot on the fire -- omer ani maasai le-melekh (H559, H4639, H4428): I recite my work to the king; leshoni et sopher mahir (H3956, H5842, H5608, H4106): the tongue as a fast scribe's pen. The poet cannot get the words down quickly enough.

2.text: You are the fairest of the sons of men; grace is poured out upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
2.amp: You are fairer [yaphah -- more beautiful] than the children [ben] of men [adam]: grace [chen] is poured [yatsaq] into your lips [saphah]: therefore God [Elohim] has blessed [barak] you for ever [olam].
2.notes: yaphyaphita mi-bene adam (H3302, H1121, H120): the doubled verb -- 'beautiful-beautiful' -- fairer than any son of Adam; hutsaq chen be-siphtotekha (H3332, H2580, H8193): grace POURED onto the lips, cast like metal -- Luke 4:22's 'gracious words' on the Bridegroom's mouth. al-ken berakhekha Elohim le-olam (H1288, H430, H5769): blessed forever.

3.text: Strap your sword on your thigh, O mighty one -- your splendor and your majesty.
3.amp: Gird [chagar] your sword [chereb] upon your thigh [yarek], O most mighty [gibbor -- warrior], with your glory [hod] and your majesty [hadar].
3.notes: chagor-charbekha al-yarekh gibbor (H2296, H2719, H3409, H1368): the Bridegroom is a warrior first -- sword on the thigh -- hodekha va-hadarekha (H1935, H1926): splendor and majesty, the royal pair of Psalm 104:1, worn like the sword. Revelation 19:11-16 dresses the Rider the same way.

4.text: And in your majesty ride out victoriously for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness; let your right hand teach you awesome deeds.
4.amp: And in your majesty [hadar] ride ['prosper thou, ride thou', rakab, the KJV margin] prosperously [tsalach -- succeed, advance] because [dabar -- on the matter] of truth [emeth] and meekness [anavah -- humility] and righteousness [tsedek]; and your right hand [yamin] shall teach [yarah] you terrible things [yare -- awesome deeds].
4.notes: va-hadarekha tselach rekhab (H1926, H6743, H7392): in majesty, succeed, RIDE -- al-debar-emet ve-anvah-tsedek (H1697, H571, H6037, H6664): on behalf of truth and humble righteousness -- the King's war aims are virtues. ve-torekha noraot yeminekha (H3384, H3372, H3225): let Your right hand teach You awesome deeds -- the hand that does the wonders is the hand that learns them.

5.text: Your arrows are sharp -- peoples fall beneath you -- in the heart of the King's enemies.
5.amp: Your arrows [chets] are sharp [shanan] in the heart [leb] of the king's [melek] enemies [oyeb]; whereby the people [am] fall [naphal] under you.
5.notes: chitsekha shenunim (H2671, H8150): sharpened arrows -- ammim tachtekha yippelu (H5971, H5307): peoples fall under you -- be-leb oyebe ha-melekh (H3820, H341, H4428): in the heart of the King's enemies. The Hebrew word order puts the falling peoples in the middle of the arrow's flight; the conquest is by the heart.

6.text: Your throne, O God, stands forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness is the scepter of Your kingdom.
6.amp: Your throne [kisse], O God [Elohim], is for ever [olam] and ever [ad]: the sceptre [shebet] of Your kingdom [malkut] is a right [mishor -- level, upright] sceptre.
6.notes: kisakha Elohim olam va-ed (H3678, H430, H5769, H5703): the King addressed as GOD -- the line Hebrews 1:8 quotes of the Son: 'But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever'. shebet mishor shebet malkhutekha (H7626, H4334, H4438): a scepter of levelness -- straight rule, Psalm 67:4's mishor. The verse the church has always read as the Messiah's divinity in the Psalter.

7.text: You have loved righteousness and You have hated wickedness; that is why God, Your own God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness above Your companions.
7.amp: You love [ahab] righteousness [tsedek], and hate [sane] wickedness [resha]: therefore God [Elohim], Your God, has anointed [mashach] You with the oil [shemen] of gladness [sason] above Your fellows [chaber -- companions].
7.notes: ahabta tsedek va-tisna resha (H157, H6664, H8130, H7562): the King's character, the ground of the anointing -- al-ken meshachakha Elohim Elohekha (H4886, H430): therefore God, YOUR God, anointed You -- God addressed as God in verse 6 and yet having a God in verse 7: the Son and the Father in one couplet, which is exactly how Hebrews 1:9 reads it. shemen sason me-chaberekha (H8081, H8342, H2270): the oil of gladness beyond the companions -- the Messiah, the Anointed One, more anointed than any king before Him.

8.text: All your robes are myrrh and aloes and cassia; out of ivory palaces the strings have made you glad.
8.amp: All your garments [beged] smell of myrrh [mor], and aloes [ahalim], and cassia [qetsiah], out of the ivory [shen] palaces [hekal], whereby [men -- strings, stringed instruments; read 'from which' by the KJV] they have made you glad [samach].
8.notes: mor-va-ahalot qetsiot kol-bigdotekha (H4753, H174, H7102, H899): the wedding robes so drenched in spice they ARE myrrh and aloes -- the Song of Songs' perfumes -- min-hekhle shen (H1964, H8127): from palaces of ivory, ivory-paneled halls like Ahab's ivory house (cf. 1 Kings 22:39); minni simmechukha (H4482, H8055): from there they gladdened you -- the WEB reads the strings, the stringed instruments, playing him in.

9.text: Kings' daughters are among your honored women; at your right hand stands the queen in the gold of Ophir.
9.amp: Kings' [melek] daughters [bath] were among your honourable women [yaqar -- precious ones]: upon your right hand [yamin] did stand [natsab] the queen [shegal -- the royal consort] in gold [kethem -- fine gold] of Ophir [Ophir].
9.notes: benot melakhim be-yiqqerotekha (H1323, H4428, H3368): princesses among his precious ones, the court -- nitsevah shegal li-minekha (H5324, H7694, H3225): the shegal, the queen consort, STATIONED at his right hand -- be-khetem Ophir (H3800, H211): in Ophir's gold, proverbial in Israel for the finest gold (Job 28:16; Isaiah 13:12). The bride enters the poem dressed for the throne.

10.text: Listen, O daughter; look, and bend your ear: forget your own people and your father's house,
10.amp: Hearken [shama], O daughter [bath], and consider [raah -- see], and incline [natah] your ear [ozen]; forget [shakach] also your own people [am], and your father's [ab] house [bayith];
10.notes: shimi-bat u-rei ve-hatti oznekh (H8085, H1323, H7200, H5186, H241): three imperatives to the bride -- hear, see, bend the ear -- ve-shikhchi ammekh u-bet abikh (H7911, H5971, H1004, H1): forget your people and your father's house: Genesis 2:24's leaving, from the bride's side, and Abraham's call in Genesis 12:1. The church has long applied this counsel to brides -- and, following Ephesians 5:31-32, to itself as the Bride who leaves all for Christ.

11.text: and the King will long for your beauty. Because he is your lord, bow down to him.
11.amp: So shall the king [melek] greatly desire [avah -- long for] your beauty [yophi]: for he is your Lord [adon]; and worship [shachah -- bow down] you him.
11.notes: ve-yit'av ha-melekh yophyekh (H183, H4428, H3308): the King will CRAVE your beauty -- the leaving of verse 10 is answered by desire -- ki-hu adonayikh (H113): for he is your lord -- ve-hishtachavi-lo (H7812): bow to him. Sarah's 'lord' of 1 Peter 3:6, and the bride's posture before the Bridegroom-King.

12.text: The daughter of Tyre will come with a gift; the rich ones of the people will come courting your favor.
12.amp: And the daughter [bath] of Tyre [Tsor] shall be there with a gift [minchah -- tribute]; even the rich [ashir] among the people [am] shall intreat [chalah -- seek the favor of] your favour ['face', panim, the KJV margin].
12.notes: u-bat-Tsor be-minchah (H1323, H6865, H4503): the daughter of Tyre -- the richest city on the coast, Hiram's Tyre -- bringing tribute; panayikh yechallu ashire am (H6440, H2470, H6223, H5971): the margin's 'face' -- the wealthy softening the bride's face with gifts. The nations courting the queen: Isaiah 60's caravans in a wedding procession.

13.text: The King's daughter within is all glory; her clothing is woven with gold.
13.amp: The king's [melek] daughter [bath] is all glorious [kebuddah -- weighty with glory] within [penimah -- inside]: her clothing [lebush] is of wrought [mishbetsot -- settings, filigree] gold [zahab].
13.notes: kol-kebuddah bat-melekh penimah (H3520, H1323, H4428, H6441): all glorious, the king's daughter, WITHIN -- the inner room where she is dressed, and, as the church has read it, the inner beauty of 1 Peter 3:4 -- mi-mishbetsot zahab lebushah (H4865, H2091, H3830): her dress of gold filigree, the settings that hold jewels.

14.text: In embroidered robes she is led to the King; the virgins behind her, her companions, are brought to you.
14.amp: She shall be brought [yabal -- led along] unto the king [melek] in raiment of needlework [riqmah -- embroidery]: the virgins [betulah] her companions [reah] that follow [achar] her shall be brought [bo] unto you.
14.notes: li-rqamot tubal la-melekh (H7553, H2986, H4428): in embroideries she is LED to the king -- yabal, the procession-verb -- betulot achareha reoteha (H1330, H310, H7464): the maidens behind her, her friends, mubaot lakh (H935): brought to you. The bridal party of Matthew 25's ten virgins.

15.text: With gladness and rejoicing they are led along; they enter the King's palace.
15.amp: With gladness [simchah] and rejoicing [gil] shall they be brought [yabal]: they shall enter [bo] into the king's [melek] palace [hekal].
15.notes: tubalnah bi-semachot va-gil (H2986, H8057, H1524): led with gladness and exultation -- tevoenah be-hekhal melekh (H935, H1964, H4428): into the king's palace. The procession ends inside; Revelation 19:9's marriage supper is this verse's destination.

16.text: In place of your fathers will be your sons; you will make them princes in all the earth.
16.amp: Instead of your fathers [ab] shall be your children [ben], whom you may make [shith -- appoint] princes [sar] in all the earth [eretz].
16.notes: tachat abotekha yihyu banekha (H1, H1121): the poet turns back to the king -- sons in place of fathers, the dynasty secured -- teshitemo le-sarim be-khol-ha-aretz (H7896, H8269, H776): princes in ALL the earth: for David's line, a hope; for the Son of David, the many sons brought to glory (cf. Hebrews 2:10; Revelation 5:10).

17.text: I will cause your name to be remembered in every generation; therefore the peoples will give you thanks forever and ever.
17.amp: I will make your name [shem] to be remembered [zakar] in all generations ['to generation and generation', dor va-dor]: therefore shall the people [am] praise [yadah -- give thanks to] you for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
17.notes: azkirah shimkha be-khol-dor va-dor (H2142, H8034, H1755): the poet's own vow -- to keep the name in memory generation after generation -- al-ken ammim yehodukha le-olam va-ed (H5971, H3034, H5769, H5703): therefore the PEOPLES, plural, will thank you forever. A court poet promised a king immortality; three thousand years on, the nations are still singing this psalm to its true King.
